subject: How to use multipliers to estimate density of rare species

messages.author: 783409cf000e6519
messages.subject: How to use multipliers to estimate density of rare species
parts:
Hello,

I'm new to Distance and have been analysing multi species surveys. I want to use multipliers to get an estimate of the density of a rarer species in the study area. 
I will be using the detection probability, SE and df from an analysis of a more numerous species that is similiar in behaviour but I have a couple of questions:

In the Help pages, it says to perform a normal distance analysis so I assume I pick the detection probability etc from the model that performs the best and that it doesn't have to be a Uniform model?

The detection probability listed at the bottom of the Density estimates/global part of the results was 50.5, should the multiplier then be 0.505?

My data is in intervals, it that a problem?

Under the multiplier tab, I assume I pick the multiply option (*)?


Thanks in advance

Borgny

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to use multipliers to estimate density of rare species
parts:
Borgny

To perform what you request, follow these steps:
  • analyse the "abundant" species using a data filter to include only that species in your analysis.  Select the most appropriate model for those data and record P, SE(P), and degrees of freedom from that analysis
    • the value of P is reported by Distance as a quantity < 1, for example in this output:
    •                          Estimate      %CV     df     95% Confidence Interval
                              ------------------------------------------------------
      Uniform/Cosine        
                       p      0.41914       23.30   130.00 0.26593      0.66061   
    • so there should be no need to multiply by 100,
    • however, you will need find SE(P) elsewhere in the output:
    •             Point        Standard    Percent Coef.        95 Percent
        Parameter   Estimate       Error      of Variation     Confidence Interval
        ---------  -----------  -----------  --------------  ----------------------
            p        0.41914      0.97676E-01      23.30      0.26593      0.66061   


  • create a new data filter for the rare species
  • enter the P, SE(P) and degrees of freedom from previous analysis in the multipliers fields of the global layer of the project
    • however, use the division "/" sign as the number of detections will be divided by P.  P < 1, meaning the resulting quotient will be a quantity larger than the number detected--thereby accounting for imperfect detectability
  • fit a uniform key function with no adjustments to the rare species
    • the multiplier in Distance will produce an estimate of the number of animals of the rare species
There is no inherent difficulty with performing this analysis with binned (interval) distance data.
